guards.what: N: the power's sole applier is Speed Potion -- a PORTED potion, not a scope boundary (SpeedPotion.cs:26-31 vs sts2_rl/potions.py:127-144)
guards.rationale:
RE-VERDICTED 2026-07-26 (potion-scope re-verdict pass), from waiver. The shared contract's 'Out of scope everywhere: potions (deferred by Perry)' has been DELETED on Perry's instruction ("don't ignore potions anymore"). `potion` is now an ordinary audit kind -- 51 sim units, audit/records/potion/, `harness.py roster potion` -- and it is UNAUDITED, exactly like `monster`. The previous pass had already narrowed this guard until the only thing left standing on the clause was 'there is no audit/records/potion/ tier for this potion to live in'. That sentence is no longer a scope statement, it is a coverage statement, and coverage is not a waiver. So the guard is re-derived on its merits: the applier potion is read in full against its C# model and verdicted here.
THE APPLIER IS FAITHFUL, AND IT CARRIES THE SAME WRAPPER TRAP AS FLEX POTION. src/Core/Models/Potions/SpeedPotion.cs:22 declares CanonicalVars = new PowerVar<DexterityPower>(5m) -- typed on DexterityPower -- while SpeedPotion.cs:30 applies `PowerCmd.Apply<SpeedPotionPower>(choiceContext, target, baseValue, base.Owner.Creature, null)`, i.e. the temporary WRAPPER, with the DexterityPower var only supplying the number. Reading the var as the applied class would give permanent Dexterity instead of the end-of-turn-reverting kind. sts2_rl/potions.py:141-144 applies SpeedPotionPower with DEXTERITY = 5 (sts2_rl/potions.py:137), so it takes the wrapper. No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension in the file, so 5 is the pinned non-ascension value. APPLIER: C#'s fourth argument is `base.Owner.Creature` (parameter `Creature? applier`, src/Core/Commands/PowerCmd.cs:101), matching `applier=ctx.player`; cardSource is null on both sides. TargetType.AnyPlayer (SpeedPotion.cs:20) and AssertValidForTargetedPotion (SpeedPotion.cs:28) are the multiplayer target-validity path, waived as multiplayer; ExtraHoverTips (SpeedPotion.cs:24) is presentation. Rarity Common (SpeedPotion.cs:16) matches the sim's class default (sts2_rl/potions.py:34). REACHABILITY IS ESTABLISHED, NOT WAIVED (binding rule 6): @register_potion puts it in ALL_POTIONS and it is in the generation pool at sts2_rl/potion_pools.py:61 (common); the conformance runner asserts the belt slot by slot (sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py:625-631). WHAT IS STILL NOT JUDGED HERE is a coverage fact, not a verdict: `potion/speed_potion` has no record yet because the whole potion kind is unaudited. Nothing in this record depends on it.

guards.what: The Dexterity leg's own observable consequence, as distinct from the family's slot verdict
guards.issue: RE-DERIVED 2026-07-26 (review fix pass). Stated separately so the AfterSideTurnEnd verdict above is not read as more proven than it is, and re-labelled from an admission that the consequence is "UNPROVEN" to a positive dormancy argument with a named trigger. The SLOT gap is the same code path power/setup_strike executed, so the verdict is inherited under rule 3 -- but setup_strike's witness is a DAMAGE witness (Stampede auto-plays an ATTACK from its own on_player_turn_end, so it sees the reverted Strength). Dexterity modifies BLOCK, so an equivalent witness needs a POWERED block gain landing strictly between combat.py:654 (on_player_turn_end, where the sim reverts) and combat.py:665 (after_player_turn_end, the correct slot). **ENUMERATED 2026-07-26; there is none.** (1) Dexterity's only consumer in the sim is DexterityPower.modify_block_additive (powers.py:129-137), and BlockCmd.apply dispatches the block-modifier families ONLY when `is_powered_attack(props)` (cmds.py:145-147), which is `MOVE in props and UNPOWERED not in props` (valueprops.py:47-49). (2) All four ported turn-end block relics pass `props=ValueProp.UNPOWERED` and therefore skip Dexterity entirely: relics/orichalcum.py:22-25, relics/cloak_clasp.py:19-24, relics/fake_orichalcum.py:25-30, relics/ripple_basin.py:36-39. (3) An AST sweep of every `on_player_turn_end` in sts2_rl finds exactly two bodies that mention block: PlatingPower._gain_block (powers.py:1058-1070), also ValueProp.UNPOWERED and owner-filtered, and ImbalancedPower's `_blocked_this_turn = False` reset (powers.py:1820), which gains none. (4) `_process_turn_end_cards` (combat.py:352-376) runs only the ethereal exhaust pass and the ten ported `on_turn_end_in_hand` bodies (bad_luck, beckon, burn, decay, doubt, infection, regret, shame, toxic, wither), and an AST sweep finds not one of them gains block. So: MECHANISM live and inherited; the DEXTERITY LEG DORMANT. **NAMED TRIGGER:** any ported effect that gains POWERED block (props MOVE without UNPOWERED -- i.e. card block, or a relic/power turn-end gain that drops the UNPOWERED prop) strictly between combat.py:654 and combat.py:665; concretely, a turn-end-in-hand card that gains card block, or an Orichalcum/Cloak Clasp-shaped relic ported without the UNPOWERED prop. Whoever fixes the family (one line: on_player_turn_end -> after_player_turn_end) fixes both legs regardless.

notes: HARNESS, not a verdict (moved out of `guards` 2026-07-26 in the review fix pass): harness.py's list_overrides enumerated ONE hook for this unit -- OriginModel, the only member the .cs file itself declares -- where the unit needs six, because it did not follow the C# base class. The five inherited hooks in this record's `hooks` section were added by hand; validation accepts extra keys. This is defect 2b of the stream report's section 8, found by half A on six TemporaryStrengthPower subclasses and reproducing on both previously unauditable potion powers. It used to be recorded as a guard verdicted `waiver`, which was wrong: a tooling defect is not a scope exclusion, and binding rule 1 reserves `waiver` for genuinely out-of-scope material (multiplayer / presentation / ascension / other characters). It is a note about the audit apparatus, not a sim-vs-game finding, so it carries no verdict and does not enter this record's rollup.
